title: Piron band engagements and the Roosevelt Hotel broadcasts
summary: Piron's band played country clubs and Jefferson Highway nightclubs, then the Roosevelt in 1932 with a WSMB broadcast.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: mostly old blues such as the numbers they're using are like Panama Maple Leaf and High Society and this this number you call that this number here we're playing every day in our year they're using it for commercial music mostly it's the Muscat Rama all them numbers like Panama Maple Leaf High Society and we all in them days called them old Scott Joplin that's another thing that's considered as the red book this man from Scott Joplin from Chicago he had all written that music and mostly two-quote music and here people down here take it and just break it up to our way you know what I mean just swing it the jazz band and that's during the later years from when I first went in the P-Rom band that was later part of 28 and that's where we started playing at the just that weekend at the country club and later on we went to a place that's called Jack Sheen's Suburban Garden Night you know what I mean it was a trench unit's nightclub on the old Jefferson Highway and we worked out there 18 months and left from there went over to a place that's called the Suburban Garden that's on the Jefferson Highway again we worked out there it's been two years with P-Rom band then we left there we worked there all through up to the 30s and we went at the Hotel Roosevelt and worked there from January the 9th of 1932 that turned them there to call it the Venetian room and we worked there from 32 January the 9th to April the 22nd of the same year
